content.title: Shutdown Cuts Off Flood Insurance Program During Storm Season
content.summary: In areas that require flood insurance to close a loan, that’s a problem.  As the government shutdown continues for a second week, with no sign of breakthrough on the horizon, the coverage gap is poised to keep widening.  As many as 1,400 sales per day could stall or fall through without flood insurance, the National Association of Realtors estimates.

content.title: Bessent says US ended fiscal 2025 with lower deficit-to-GDP ratio
content.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US ended fiscal year 2025 with a lower deficit-to-GDP ratio than the year before. He sounded an optimistic note for 2026, noting that the US is on its way to lowering deficits without causing a recession.

content.summary: Banks trying to navigate the nation's capital during the Trump era are getting both political pushback and sweeping reforms that could work to their advantage.

content.title: S&P 500 Movers: Equifax Hits Back At FICO In Credit Score Wars
content.summary: Equifax has slashed prices for mortgage credit scores in response to Fair Isaac's move last week that aimed to limit the mortgage industry's reliance on credit bureaus.  Fair Isaac, known as FICO, was the biggest laggard on the S&P 500, giving back a big chunk of last week's gains, while Equifax recovered some of last week's losses.  The backdrop is that FICO has been under pressure from Bill Pulte, director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, who said in July that government-backed mortgage giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will now allow lenders to use VantageScore 4.0 as an alternative to the traditional FICO score.

content.title: Trump Call for Fannie, Freddie to Spur Building Is ‘Mystery’
content.summary: Trump asked the two government-controlled firms, which together back more than half the residential mortgage market, to “get big homebuilders going” in a Truth Social post on Sunday, but didn’t elaborate on what he had in mind.  Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte, Fannie and Freddie’s regulator and conservator, shared the post on X and vowed that he was “on it.”
